description: Read-only access to the point-in-time Longbridge archive (#2575): the capture's health, and archived values as of a past moment. The capture runs outside Neige as a systemd timer; this plugin only reads the archive and the capture's last exit, never the token, and never calls Longbridge.
planner_instructions: This read-only plugin exposes the Longbridge archive; a separate systemd timer captures it. plugin_archive_capture_status reports Core health: ok, attention or failing. Core is the original eight endpoints; snapshots, financial reports, calendar and bars are Supplemental. Show both tiers in Reports. Supplemental quota/auth failures, timeouts and gaps never require an owner question. Overall run outcome can remain open/partial after Core completes. For failing Core/host health, ask the owner with neige_user_ask, quoting the reasons, and repeat only when reasons change. For attention, disclose weaker/lost data in the Report without asking. plugin_archive_capture_watch on:true keeps this Track's live archive.status table, rendered with source neige://plugin/archive/archive.status; on:false removes it. plugin_archive_read_at returns the latest successful fetch at/before at, narrowed by a JSON pointer; call twice to compare moments. Original six endpoints began capture 2026-10-13 UTC for trading day 2026-10-12; annual and new endpoint history starts only with their own captures. Never infer archive history from a fiscal period or trade date. No successful fetch yields no_value; never planned yields not_archived. Calendar uses market:US; other endpoints use symbol. Financial reports are summaries: do not invent missing TBVPS, finance-lease additions or segment revenue. Align stock/benchmark bars by explicit trade_date; never substitute an older benchmark session. Calendar reported_counts are provider statistics, not returned-event cardinality; variants may normalize. Group dates are upstream labels and can differ from ext.local_date/datetime; do not infer NY earnings timing from group keys.

exposes_tools.name: capture_status
exposes_tools.description: The archive's health now: ok, attention or failing, every reason, how the last capture start ended, and the last 7 runs with their pair counts (ok, tried with no ok, not tried, planned) and index membership. failing: recent Core capture ended partial or degraded (fewer than half its Core pairs ok) and no later day has ended complete since, missed days included; the last start had no usable token or stopped on a fatal error; no start has recorded its exit for longer than the configured bound; or the archive cannot be read. attention: partial or degraded Core that a later complete Core day followed, a recent day was missed, Core ended complete with pairs that have no ok, the latest universe is not observed, or the missed-day scan was incomplete. Reads local files only. Per-run core/supplemental counts, core_outcome/core_finished_at, total counts and endpoint tier classifications are returned. Supplemental gaps never change health; overall outcome still describes all capture.

exposes_tools.name: read_at
exposes_tools.description: What the archive held at a past moment: for each read, the body of the latest successful fetch of that symbol and endpoint at or before `at`, at the JSON pointer. A later fetch is invisible, a failed fetch never replaces an earlier value, and an empty-shaped body is a value. Each read answers result value (with as_of, the capture's trading day, and fetched_at, UTC), not_archived (the archive never planned this symbol and endpoint), no_value (planned, but nothing fetched by `at`; the original six endpoints began capture 2026-10-13 UTC, for trading day 2026-10-12; annual starts only with its own first capture) or pointer_missing (the body has nothing at the pointer). Bodies are large (consensus ~20 KB, forecast_eps ~26 KB, rating_detail ~51 KB, valuation ~14 KB); an answer over 40 KiB fails with each read's size, so select with a pointer. Body shapes: consensus (default quarterly) and consensus_annual (period_type=af) {list[{fiscal_year, fiscal_period, period_text, details[{key, name, estimate, actual, ...}]}], current_index, currency, opt_periods, current_period}; forecast_eps {items[{forecast_eps_median, forecast_eps_mean, forecast_eps_lowest, forecast_eps_highest, institution_total, institution_up, institution_down, forecast_start_date, forecast_end_date}]}; rating_latest {evaluate{buy, over, hold, under, sell, no_opinion, total, start_date, end_date}, target{highest_price, lowest_price, prev_close, start_date, end_date}, industry_*}; ratings {evaluate{strong_buy, buy, hold, sell, under, date}, recommend, target, change, ccy_symbol, updated_at}; rating_detail {evaluate{list[{strong_buy, buy, hold, sell, under, no_opinion, date}]}, target{updated_at, prediction_accuracy, data_percent, list[{timestamp, price, meet, avg_target, min_target, max_target, date}]}, ccy_symbol}; valuation {metrics{pe{low, median, high, desc, list[...]}}, range}. Reads local files only. New endpoints: earnings_snapshot {report, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, fp_start, fp_end, currency, fo_revenue, fo_ebit, fo_eps, fr_*}; financial_reports {report, symbol, list{IS,BS,CF}}, each kind has indicators[].accounts[{field,name,values[{year,fp_end,period,value,...}]}]. These are standardized summaries, not full filings; absent TBVPS, lease additions or segments must not be invented. daily_candlesticks is a typed projection {format:daily_bars_v1, symbol, timezone:America/New_York, adjust:none, session:regular, start,end,bars[{trade_date,timestamp,open,high,low,close,volume,turnover}]}; prices are decimal strings, at most six closes. Read stock and benchmark in one call, align by trade_date, report missing sessions. finance_calendar uses market:US instead of symbol and returns {format:earnings_calendar_v1,market,start,end,days{YYYY-MM-DD:{SYMBOL:{EVENT_ID:event}}},pages[{date,offset,fetched_at,raw_json}]}; select /days/YYYY-MM-DD/SYMBOL for a small answer. Empty calendar days are explicit. New data begins only with its first successful capture. Daily snapshots can precede later upstream earnings updates. Calendar coverage=upstream_group_company_dates is published company/group-label coverage, not exhaustive fiscal variants or verified NY event dates. reported_counts are provider statistics, not the number of returned IDs; company_counts describe published companies. pages also record the actual requested count. Group labels, event date/datetime and ext.local_date can disagree; preserve and inspect them rather than infer a NY date.

at.description: The moment to read at: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, such as 2026-10-13T16:00:00-04:00.

symbol.description: The security symbol as archived, such as NVDA.US.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the body, such as /target/highest_price; "" for the whole body.

market.description: Market target for finance_calendar; omit symbol.

exposes_tools.name: capture_watch
exposes_tools.description: Start (on: true) or stop (on: false) keeping the live archive.status table on the calling Track. The table refreshes on the plugin's own poll, only when the status changes; stopping deletes it from this Track.

on.description: true to show the table on this Track, false to remove it

data_dir.description: Absolute path of the capture job's data dir (its config's data_dir). The plugin reads archive.sqlite3 read-only and last_exit.json there, and nothing else.

poll_seconds.description: Seconds between status reads for watching Tracks (10 to 3600).

stale_after_minutes.description: Minutes after the last recorded capture exit at which the status says the timer is not starting the capture (60 to 2880). It must exceed 30 (the timer's interval) plus the capture's attempt_timeout_minutes, with a margin: a start can hold the lock that long, and a start that finds the lock held records nothing. The default 90 fits attempt_timeout_minutes up to about 45.
